title: How to redefine coredns return code

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: There are some external plugins that support your implied use case. Eg _alternate_  https://github.com/coredns/alternate

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: I am assuming the implied use case is that you want incoming queries to try one upstream server first, then if that response is   does not have a positive result, discard that result and try a second upstream server.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
What’s the underlying problem you are trying to solve with the proposed solution. Eg why do you want to do this. Why do you expect your upstream servers hold different sets of records?

If one resolves public domains, and the other resolves a private domain, then the proper way to handle this is by creating a server block for your private domain, routing queries based on their domain, instead of trying to implement a sort of cascading chain of forwards.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> I am assuming the implied use case is that you want incoming queries to try one upstream server first, then if that response is does not have a positive result, discard that result and try a second upstream server.

thx @participant1 .

The scene I encountered was a bit special. There are two network cards on pod A, which come from different VPCs. One of the network cards communicates with the CoreDNS.

The pod A needs to access a special domain name. This domain name needs to pass through the DNS of the other network card to have correct resolution. Therefore, the resolv.conf of pod A configures two nameservers, one of which is the clusterip of CoreDNS, and the other is the dns server corresponding to another VPC. 

It is hoped here that in pod A, after accessing CoreDNS domain name resolution fails, go to another nameserver to try again. The premise is that CoreDNS domain name resolution needs to return `SERVFAIL`.

I don't know if my description is clear. ^_^

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: If I understand correctly, the proper DNS way to do this would be to also give coredns access to both DNS servers, and configure it to forward queries for that "special" (i.e. private?) domain to the VPC dns server.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> It is hoped here that in pod A, after accessing CoreDNS domain name resolution fails, go to another nameserver to try again. The premise is that CoreDNS domain name resolution needs to return SERVFAIL.

I expect this approach may cause unexpected results elsewhere. E.g. it may short circuit (break) resolv.conf query domain suffix searching.  I think it would also cause problems for some clients that do parallel A/AAAA queries, and "Happy Eyeballs".

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Since the proposed solution is hacky and will break other things, take care to only apply it to the "special" domain in question.

There is an open PR to add response code rewrite to the the _rewrite_ plugin. #6204. This should be able to implement the solution you propose.

CoreDNS doesnt have to have direct access to the VPC, It could instead forward to another dns service in the cluster that has a Pod in the VPC (like your "Pod A").
